en: The Philippine government mandates quarterly earthquake drills because the country sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, teaching students practical drop, cover, and hold safety skills.
The Department of Health promotes lagundi leaves for coughs, validating the traditional herbal medicine practices of indigenous Filipinos with modern scientific research.
PAGASA issues typhoon wind signals to help local government units enforce practical evacuation safety and protect coastal communities from severe storm surges.
The Philippine national fruit, the mango, contains high levels of Vitamin C, which practically helps children boost their immune systems against common illnesses.
National hero Jose Rizal advocated for public health and sanitation in the Philippines, emphasizing clean water and proper waste disposal to prevent cholera outbreaks.
The indigenous Banaue Rice Terraces demonstrate ancient soil conservation science, practically preventing landslides and erosion during the heavy rainy seasons in the Cordilleras.
During the Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate homes with edible kiping made from rice, providing a safe, food-grade alternative to synthetic plastic decorations.
The Philippine Constitution guarantees the right to a healthful ecology, empowering citizens to report illegal logging that causes dangerous flash floods and landslides.
National Scientist Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a sanitary bamboo incubator, providing a safe, non-electric way to keep premature rural babies warm and healthy.
The Land Transportation Office mandates wearing standard motorcycle helmets to practically prevent severe traumatic brain injuries during road accidents across the Philippines.
The traditional Filipino practice of herbal steam inhalation uses hot water vapor to safely clear nasal congestion without needing synthetic over-the-counter cold medicines.
The Bureau of Fire Protection teaches the practical Stop, Drop, and Roll technique in schools to protect children from severe burn injuries during fires.
